actual_tasks: Determine whether opposite direction is an equivalence relation on all rays of a plane.
source_reviews.independent_solution: No. The relation is symmetric but not reflexive and not transitive. A nonzero direction d is not opposite itself. For r=R((0,0),(1,0)), s=R((0,0),(-1,0)), t=R((1,0),(1,0)), r is opposite s and s is opposite t, whereas r and t are same-direction rather than opposite. Negating -d to d proves symmetry. Pairs with nonparallel, noncoincident supports are unrelated, without changing the domain of all rays.
domain_cases: All genuine nondegenerate rays of a plane form the domain.
A transitivity counterexample may use distinct same-direction first and third rays.
The relation need not hold for every pair in the domain.
capacity_limits: A bare negative choice does not demonstrate testing all three equivalence axioms or constructing a transitivity witness.

coverage.evidence: The independent axiom analysis is complete, but its retention in a choice task is unreviewed without views.

If L=line OM, its image support equals L iff P is on L, and is a distinct parallel line iff P is outside L. source_reviews.independent_solution: Write the first pair as R(X,d) and R(Y,-d) after choosing a common nonzero direction representative. With C=(X+Y)/2, H_C(X+t*d)=Y-t*d for all t>=0, so the whole first ray maps exactly to the second. Endpoint correspondence forces 2C-X=Y, proving uniqueness of the center. If X=Y, C is that endpoint. P on the support gives the same support; P off it gives a distinct parallel support.

actual_tasks: Classify counts of parallel unordered side pairs in a convex quadrilateral.
Classify counts of parallel unordered side pairs in a convex pentagon.
Classify counts of parallel unordered side pairs in a convex hexagon.
Determine and justify whether an odd-sided polygon can have a symmetry center.
source_reviews.independent_solution: For nondegenerate convex polygons with genuine corners, each unoriented side direction has at most two sides, on the two extreme supporting lines. Parallel pairs therefore use disjoint pairs of sides, giving at most floor(n/2). Attainable counts are {0,1,2}, {0,1,2}, {0,1,2,3} for n=4,5,6; maxima are 2,2,3, not each polygon's exact count. Count zero is attained by cyclically joining the first n points (x,x^2), x=1,2,4,8,16,32: all side slopes, including the closing edge, are different sums of two powers of two. Exact positive-count convex coordinate witnesses are recorded below and in SOURCE-FIRST.md. Under central symmetry, genuine corners pair in two-element orbits. A corner cannot be fixed at the center, since its two incident edge directions would have to be negatives of each other and hence collinear. Thus an ordinary nondegenerate odd-sided polygon has no center; the argument also covers simple concave polygons with genuine corners. Allowing redundant straight-angle vertices invalidates an unconditional claim: a rectangle with only its top side subdivided has a five-edge description, three parallel pairs on distinct supports, and a centrally symmetric represented region.
